question: Should OpenClaw support a destination-agent-specific subagent concurrency contract, and if so should it live at `agents.list[].subagents.maxConcurrent` with an effective limit composed with the existing global cap?
rationale: The requested capability adds a public configuration surface and requires an enduring semantic choice about inheritance and how two concurrency limits compose; this cannot be safely inferred from an implementation detail alone.

options.title: Adopt nested per-agent subagent cap
options.body: Add `agents.list[].subagents.maxConcurrent` and enforce the minimum of this value and the global subagent limit across supported spawn paths.

options.title: Keep global-only scheduling
options.body: Retain the current global cap and document separate gateway processes or workload partitioning as the supported isolation boundary.

options.title: Fold into broader lane design
options.body: Defer this narrow setting until maintainers choose a unified model for named subagent lanes and per-agent scheduling.

recommendation.title: Adopt nested per-agent subagent cap
recommendation.body: Add `agents.list[].subagents.maxConcurrent` and enforce the minimum of this value and the global subagent limit across supported spawn paths.
